mutants.description: The S_RUN window and its count both take the blanked comparator sample from BLANK_CLKS-1 clocks before high-side turn-on instead of BLANK_CLKS clocks before, so the run lookback is one clock short while soft start keeps the full lookback.
mutants.reason: In S_RUN, if cp_sync changes exactly BLANK_CLKS clocks before a pwm_sync rising edge (high 5 clocks back, low 4 clocks back, or the reverse), the run window records the wrong value for that cycle. fault_count_run_out and window_trip then differ from the correct design.

mutants.description: The bit leaving the run window is copied across the whole count width instead of zero-extended, so a faulted cycle that leaves the 16-cycle run window adds one to fault_count_run instead of taking one off.
mutants.reason: In S_RUN, once a faulted cycle reaches the end of the 16-cycle window and leaves, fault_count_run_out goes up instead of down. Overcurrent that has already aged out of the window can then hold window_trip high or make it trip.

mutants.description: The run window and count are also cleared on the clock after window_trip fires, as if the trip itself should start a clean window, instead of being cleared only when neither S_SS nor S_RUN is active.
mutants.reason: After the run count reaches trip_run in S_RUN, fault_count_run_out drops to 0 on the next clock without a pwm_rise, and window_trip falls while run_active is still high. In the correct design the count and the trip hold until the supervisor leaves S_RUN.
